articles.title: A gold pocket watch recovered from a Titanic passenger sells for over $300,000
articles.summary: The Titanic sank after striking an iceberg in the North Atlantic on 15 April 1912 [PA Media] Rare items belonging to passengers of the Titanic have been sold at auction for record-breaking sums. The highest selling artefacts were a pocket watch from third-class passenger Mary Mangan, which fetched £250,000, and a diamond ring worn by famous passenger Lady Duff Gordon, which was bought for £140,000. Another item was a detailed, water-stained letter recovered from the body of its writer, first-class passenger Ramon Artagaveytia Gomez, which was auctioned for £80,000. Auctioneer Andrew Aldridge from Henry Aldridge and Son in Devizes, Wiltshire, said the "epic sale" was evidence of the lasting global interest in the tragic story. More from Wiltshire Why women have rallied behind rape victim Joanne Young Warning about scammers posing as detectives 'Replenished reservoirs' and 'landmark cases' The Titanic departed on its maiden voyage on 10 April 1912 and sank in the early hours of 15 April with the loss of about 1,500 lives. The golden watch was found on the body of 32-year-old Irish passenger Mangan, and was returned to her family alongside her other possessions. It has recently spent several weeks on exhibition alongside the rest of the Mangan Collection at Titanic Belfast. Mangan had moved to the US and had returned to Ireland in early 1912 to visit family. Written in Spanish, a letter from Ramon Artagaveytia Gomez was one of the few penned onboard by a first class passenger in a language other than English [Henry Aldridge and Sons] The rare letter, which was written onboard in Spanish on official Titanic letter-headed paper, describes the Titanic in detail from paint colours to temperature and the number of diners. It was one of more than 100 items linked to the doomed liner that were sold, including an insurance document, which fetched £27,000, and a rare ticket , which sold for £45,500. Another was a postcard written by Jack Phillips , a senior wireless operator who died in the disaster after heroic actions. Phillips remained at his post sending wireless distress calls and helped to coordinate rescue efforts as the ship went down. The postcard, which was written four days earlier to his sister Elsie, was sold for nearly £32,000. The auctioneer said the postcard was particularly significant as it was written while the Titanic was docked in Southampton [Henry Aldridge and Son Ltd] "The sale total was well over £1m and Titanic items made up a large part of that," Aldridge said. He said the watch broke the record for an item sold from a third-class passenger, while the ring was sold for the highest amount ever for a piece of jewellery from the Titanic "The interest in the story is global, my clients come form all four corners of the world," he said. "I think the prices reflect the enduring interest in the subject and what we're doing with these items is keeping individuals' memories alive," he added. articles.title: Visitors leave tributes after Fiona the hippo dies in freak accident at Cincinnati Zoo
articles.summary: A necropsy has revealed that the knit cap responsible for the death of the Cincinnati Zoo's famed hippo Fiona was lodged so deep in her digestive tract that she effectively had no chance of survival. Zoo officials said on Friday that the hat got stuck 25 feet beyond Fiona's final stomach compartment and 50 feet from the end of her intestines. "Upper and lower GI endoscopy were unable to reach the object," explained Mike Wenninger, the zoo's director of animal health. "The location and anatomy made laparoscopic removal impossible. No treatment aside from supportive care had any chance for success, and the necropsy confirmed that no amount of supportive care would have worked." Fiona's mother, Bibi, and the zoo's other hippos, Tucker and Fritz, "are eating and behaving normally," said Christina Gorsuch, the zoo's director of animal care. "It's difficult to know how they're feeling, but they appear to be their normal selves." "Keepers, vets, staff, and volunteers are shaken and trying to navigate this loss," the zoo said. "She meant a lot to a lot of people." It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency. https://t.co/X0GVbDAiEQ pic.twitter.com/7wLF0uclWB — Cincinnati Zoo (@CincinnatiZoo) November 19, 2026 The zoo announced Fiona's death on Thursday, 11 days after she swallowed a hat that had slipped into her enclosure.  She was 9 years old. "It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency," the zoo said in a statement. Fans near and far have been grieving ever since. Thane Maynard, executive chair of the zoo's board, compared Fiona to "lightning in a bottle," adding that he had "never known an animal so beloved in all my life." On Friday, zoo visitors draped a hippo statue with flowers and notes written in crayon, according to the Associated Press . A young girl held up a drawing of Fiona; someone else left behind a watermelon, one of Fiona's favorite treats. Flowers, handwritten notes, watermelons and other items are displayed at a memorial for Fiona the hippo at the Cincinnati Zoo. AP Photo/Obed Lamy Flowers and cards rest by a statue outside the Cincinnati Zoo. AP Photo/Sallee Ann Harrison Jessica Grieshop, who often visited Fiona with her daughters, called the hippo an inspiration for "anyone that was going through hard times." Cincinnati landmarks, including stadiums and bridges, were lit purple Thursday night in Fiona's honor. The zoo asked people not to send flowers or gifts and instead "honor Fiona by spreading love and cheer to those around you." It is accepting memorial donations . Local businesses are raising money, too. Cincinnati bakery chain Servatii is selling $1 "Fiona Donuts" this weekend, with all proceeds going to the zoo, WKRC reported . The zoo's Hippo Cove is closed through the weekend. The zoo's animal care team spent days trying to help Fiona pass the obstruction, going so far as to use a vibration plate borrowed from a horse farm to help shake it through her digestive tract. An ultrasound showed bunching in Fiona's intestines; a colonoscopy with a 9-foot scope didn't help, nor did a "giant" enema. "Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible," said Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike. "We are in shock at the moment. We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn't anymore." Specialists said surgery wasn't an option for a full-grown Nile hippopotamus. "They have a multichambered stomach for digesting plants — sort of like a cow — but they don't regurgitate and chew cud like a cow does," Jack Kottwitz, an assistant professor at Michigan State University's College of Veterinary Medicine, told the Associated Press . "Those multiple chambers, tissue folds, fluid and digesting food easily 'hide' the hat, making removal with an endoscope from the stomach chambers very difficult." Hippos are also difficult to anesthetize and keep away from water as they heal. Zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley told reporters that Fiona ingested the knit hat on Nov. 8 after it was tossed in the air by a child and flung by a ceiling fan through a 1-foot opening above the viewing windows of her enclosure. "We probably couldn't make that happen again if we tried," Curley said at the time. "It was clearly an accident." In the days that followed, Fiona's appetite started to wane. Fiona was no stranger to health struggles; she became a sensation after she was born six weeks premature in 2017. At the time, she couldn't stand on her own and weighed just 29 pounds; the next smallest Nile hippo on record weighed roughly twice as much at birth. Fiona in 2020. John Minchillo/AP No one expected Fiona to survive. Zoo staff had to bottle-feed her with a mixture of formula and her mother's milk. (A hippopotamus had never been hand-milked before.) While teething, Fiona began to refuse the bottle, and clinicians from Cincinnati Children's Hospital were called in to administer fluids intravenously. But eventually Fiona began to thrive. Named after Shrek's love interest, Princess Fiona — zoo staff thought her ears had a similar shape — she went on to star in her own show on YouTube and other platforms. Her plight — and her adorable triumph over adversity — inspired a host of children's books, a line of beer, a bobblehead and even a limited-edition ice cream flavor. She weighed nearly 2,500 pounds when she died. Fiona also became a Cincinnati icon. Her character in the Cincinnati Ballet's 2018 production of Nutcracker reportedly " stole the show "; the same year, a Fiona mural was unveiled downtown. Fiona's death sparked a series of tributes. The Cincinnati Bengals wrote in a post on X, "Rest in peace, Fiona. The queen of the Queen City." Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno added his tribute, saying, "Fiona wasn't just Cincinnati's hippo, she was Ohio's fighter. Born tiny, premature, and against every odd, she grew up and brought pure joy to millions of us." second lady Usha Vance, the wife of Vice President JD Vance, shared an undated photo of one of their children gazing at Fiona through the glass of her enclosure. "We are so sad to hear the news about Fiona," Vance wrote. "Our family loved visiting her at the Cincinnati Zoo." "Our city is heartbroken," Mayor Aftab Pureval wrote on social media, "but we couldn't be more grateful that she was part of our lives and our community as a whole." "Our hearts are with the staff of the Cincinnati Zoo and everyone who loved her," added outgoing Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine. "She will be deeply missed." Amy Acton, Ohio's incoming governor, said that Fiona's survival story "brought joy, hope and a little extra magic to our state." On Friday, Ohio Sen. Bernie Moreno introduced a resolution honoring Fiona and the Cincinnati Zoo staff on the floor of the U.S. Senate. It passed unanimously. Fiona was Ohio’s little fighter from day one and I’m proud that my resolution honoring her passed the Senate UNANIMOUSLY. My heart goes out to the amazing team at the @CincinnatiZoo who cared for her. Rest easy, Fiona. Ohio loves you. pic.twitter.com/G0ln1rSRRF — Bernie Moreno (@berniemoreno) November 20, 2026 "Fiona was a symbol of resilience, of perseverance, and we're going to miss her in Cincinnati," Moreno said. Her loss, he added, will "leave a hole in the zoo and a hole in the heart." articles.title: FBI probes apparent hack targeting database with criminal records and more
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of a national law enforcement database that it maintains, a person familiar with the matter said Saturday. The National Crime Information Center, known as the NCIC, is a computerized database of criminal justice information that is available to local, state and federal law enforcement agencies and includes records on fugitives, missing persons, criminal history data, stolen property and other topics. The FBI declined to comment Saturday on the apparent hack, which was first reported by CNN and confirmed to The Associated Press by a person familiar with the matter who was not authorized to speak by name and spoke on the condition of anonymity. The scope of the problem was not immediately clear. Asked about the subject on Saturday, President Donald Trump said in a Fox News Channel interview: “We just heard about it, and I will say that it’s not good.” News that the NCIC was targeted comes as the country has encountered a series of digital outages in the government and private sector that Trump administration officials have said were caused by routine efforts to upgrade computer systems and fix vulnerabilities, rather than a cyberattack . There was no immediate indication that the FBI incident was related to those outages. The bureau has historically been a frequent target for hackers. In September, for instance, a criminal hacking group known as ShinyHunters revealed that it had obtained a massive trove of data on FBI employees and applicants and had compromised the bureau's jobs portal. And in March, the FBI disclosed that it was investigating “suspicious activities” on an internal system that contains sensitive information related to surveillance operations and investigations. articles.title: Trump told European leaders they were spending a lot on Ukraine, Zelensky says
articles.summary: KYIV, Nov 21 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump told European leaders this week they were spending a lot on the war in Ukraine and could use that money at home if a peace deal were reached with Russia, Ukrainian President ‌Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Saturday. Trump called into a meeting of Ukraine's Coalition of the Willing allies in Berlin on Thursday following ‌his trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping at an APEC summit in Shenzhen. "He said that Europe is spending a lot of money, and they ​could spend it on themselves after the end (of the war)," Zelenskiy, who attended the meeting in Berlin, told reporters before talks with British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting in Kyiv. "It didn't sound like a threat." Trump said on his return to Washington on Friday that Putin had clearly expressed his desire to end the war in Ukraine by  diplomatic means during their talks. But Zelenskiy said he was not convinced about Putin's intentions. "I'm a little bit more skeptical than ‌Americans that he's ready for compromises. That's what ⁠I said to the American team, by the way," he said. Putin has shown no sign of dropping his demand that Ukraine surrender all of its eastern region of Donbas in return for peace. Zelenskiy has rejected this, saying ⁠many Ukrainian soldiers have died defending land there since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022. Zelenskiy welcomed recent announcements by US envoys on including Europe as full partners in the peace process, which resumed after a nine-month hiatus with talks in Abu Dhabi this month. But he said the US envoys now needed to agree ​an ​agenda and the timing for another round of talks. "Certainly, America will try to ​make the meeting happen as soon as possible. And I ‌am confident Russia will take all steps to slightly postpone such a meeting," Zelenskiy said. Putin accused Kyiv and Europe on Thursday of not being able to make compromises to resolve the war in Ukraine. STREETING VISIT Zelenskiy reiterated on Saturday that he was ready to attend a meeting of the Group of 20 major economies, which Trump is due to host next month in Miami, and that he would be happy to hold direct talks with Putin there. So far he has not been invited. Zelenskiy said Streeting's visit, following a heavy Russian bombardment of Kyiv this week, was an important ‌show of solidarity. Putin had promised retaliation for airstrikes that crippled a major bridge ​linking Crimea, which Russia seized and annexed in 2014, to Russia's Krasnodar region this week. Zelenskiy ​dismissed Putin's assertion that the bridge had been used only ​for civilian transportation, saying a search of social media showed hundreds of images of military vehicles crossing the bridge. Zelenskiy ‌said Russia had again attacked civilian targets overnight in the ​industrial city of Kryvyi Rih - his ​hometown - where at least two people were killed, including a seven-year-old boy. Both sides denied deliberately targeting civilian infrastructure. Streeting said it was pointless for Putin to use the language of peace at international summits if his forces then bombarded civilian infrastructure. Streeting said a Russian ​violation of Polish airspace - which Polish authorities said ‌was probably by two missiles and a drone - before military exercises on Friday for the "Coalition of the Willing" was "an outrageous provocation". "The ​best response, and the response that I would appeal to all of our allies to undertake, is to do more ​to support Ukraine," he said. (Reporting by Daniel Flynn, Editing by Timothy Heritage) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/trump-told-european-leaders-were-145057566.html

articles.title: COP31 climate summit risks failure as talks go deep into overtime
articles.summary: By Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 21 (Reuters) - The COP31 climate summit will either produce a good deal or no deal at all, the European Union's top climate official said on Saturday as talks stretched deep into overtime. Negotiators from ‌nearly 200 countries are struggling to bridge divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance, delaying an agreement at the two-week conference ‌that had been scheduled to end on Friday. "It's either going to be a good deal or it's going to be no deal," EU Climate Commissioner Wopke Hoekstra told reporters. Asked about ​the chances of no deal emerging, he said: "We will find out." The last major breakdown in UN climate talks came in Copenhagen in 2009, when countries failed to adopt the Copenhagen Accord by consensus in a setback for multilateral climate diplomacy. As workers dismantled catering stands and exhibits at the venue, delegations shuttled between meeting rooms to discuss tactics, while others rested as they awaited a new version of the negotiating text. Turkey's COP31 President Murat Kurum met officials ‌from the EU, Australia and Saudi Arabia in an ⁠effort to break the deadlock, but acknowledged a deal could prove elusive. "I call on every country to act responsibly," he told reporters. "There is no benefit for anyone to ruin this process by getting hung up on words, phrases." The ⁠biggest sticking points are whether a final agreement should mention the fossil fuels driving global warming and whether it should include support for poorer countries adapting to climate change. A draft deal published on Thursday removed earlier references to ending fossil fuel use. Observers said Saudi Arabia and other major oil and gas producers ​had ​opposed the language. The draft also dropped a proposed $120 billion target for finance to help ​developing countries adapt to climate change. Negotiators had expected a ‌revised draft on Friday. But by Saturday afternoon, with no new text on the table, hopes for significant changes had faded and frustration was mounting. DELAYS Recent climate summits have regularly overrun without collapsing, eventually producing agreements. Isatou Camara, Gambia's finance negotiator, said some countries appeared to be using delay tactics to pressure others into accepting a weaker outcome. "This delay strategy which has been used at previous COPs could be so at the end when things are put on the table you accept because you are fed up, exhausted, and want to go home," she said. This year's talks have been further ‌complicated by war and rising living costs, which are competing for the attention of ​policymakers and the public. The US, the world's largest historical greenhouse gas emitter, is also ​absent from the talks for the second year in a row ​after President Donald Trump ended cooperation on climate policy, calling global warming a hoax. A UN report last month found ‌the world is on track to exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 ​degrees Fahrenheit) of warming above pre-industrial ​levels, a threshold governments agreed under the 2015 Paris Agreement to try to avoid breaching. The draft agreement acknowledges that projected overshoot and calls for faster deployment of technologies that remove greenhouse gases from the atmosphere to help bring temperatures back down. Some delegations opposed including ​carbon-removal technologies, arguing that doing so could open the ‌door to continued fossil fuel use. "The fact there is loads of unfinished business at this COP shows there's a big problem ​here," said Brenda Mwale, Malawi's loss and damage negotiator. "The question is are we in a leadership crisis? Was there really ​a vision for this COP?" (Writing by Richard Valdmanis. Editing by Mark Potter) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://ca.news.yahoo.com/cop31-climate-summit-risks-failure-143645815.html

articles.title: Trump orders federal contractors to alert White House on record requests
articles.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order late Friday instructing federal contractors to notify the White House of congressional information requests and withhold material the administration deems privileged, a move that comes as Democrats prepare to launch oversight investigations. The order applies to all federal contractors and subcontractors. Companies that fail to comply risk losing their existing contracts or being suspended from future work, according to the order. Trump framed the directive as a pushback against lawmakers whom the order accuses of "harassing private companies" to get confidential executive branch information. President Donald Trump listens during a news briefing in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room of the White House on Nov. 20, 2026, in Washington, D.C. Supreme Court Urged To Defang ‘Criminal Trap’ That Has Sent Trump Officials To Prison The order could invite legal challenges, particularly if contractors are told to withhold records sought by subpoena. Although executive privilege lets presidents protect certain internal communications, courts can intervene in clashes over congressional oversight powers. The order builds on a directive issued earlier this week by White House Counsel Will Scharf , who instructed federal agencies to clear employee congressional testimony with the administration first. Scharf added that some Democratic investigations could cross into criminal conduct, drawing pushback over what critics call a broader effort to shield the executive branch from oversight. articles.title: RFK Jr. vows to curb a measles crisis he initially underestimated
articles.summary: Hours after the United States lost its measles-elimination status, erasing a landmark public health victory earned 26 years ago, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. declared the country would fight the spread of the disease. "We will stop measles outbreaks, protect American families, and work to regain U.S. measles elimination status," Kennedy posted on X. "I continue to recommend MMR vaccination as the most effective way to prevent measles." Subscribe to The Post Most newsletter for the most important and interesting stories from The Washington Post. But as federal and state governments confront the spread of one of the world's most contagious diseases, some state and local officials question whether Kennedy and his department can bring it under control. Kennedy had sowed doubt about the safety of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine for years and, as the top U.S. health official, has sought major changes to childhood immunization policy, to cheers from some supporters of his Make America Healthy Again movement. Those actions, some public health experts say, have complicated efforts to persuade more Americans to get vaccinated and rebuild the population immunity needed to bring outbreaks under control. As federal health agencies deployed resources to West Texas in 2025, Kennedy initially underestimated the resurgence of the disease, according to two people familiar with the matter who spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe internal matters. "It took him a while to accept measles as something that wasn't going to go away quickly," said a former health official. Federal health officials must now develop a corrective action plan for the Pan American Health Organization, the regional health agency that withdrew the U.S.'s measles elimination status, outlining how the country will stop continuous spread of the virus and regain its status. PAHO officials said they expect the plan in the coming weeks, although there is no formal deadline. Even before the U.S. officially lost its designation, federal officials began taking steps toward that effort. Erica Schwartz, the director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, met earlier this month with public health groups to discuss strategies for curbing the outbreaks and to identify challenges, according to two public health officials with knowledge of the meeting who spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe private conversations. The CDC, state health officials, epidemiologists and national immunization groups are also planning regional meetings to coordinate the response, with special attention to improving outreach to vulnerable communities. The Department of Health and Human Services said it has been aggressive in fighting measles. Since August, the CDC has made $100 million available to states to improve the response. It has provided help from CDC scientists to states battling outbreaks, including Texas, South Carolina, New York, Wisconsin and Pennsylvania. "We will address PAHO's findings directly," HHS spokeswoman Emily Hilliard said in a statement. "HHS and CDC will address the findings and work with partners to document interruption of endemic transmission and meet the requirements for re-achieving elimination status." State and local health officials say they welcome those efforts. But stopping continuous spread of the virus requires a broader and sustained effort, including raising vaccination rates in communities where coverage has fallen before Kennedy came into office. Only the federal government can do what states cannot do on their own, such as coordinate across states, bring health and immunization officials together, and provide robust funding and expertise. New York's health commissioner, James McDonald, said at a briefing Thursday with reporters that PAHO's decision was expected well in advance, and a federal plan should have already been prepared. "I'm already concerned that Health and Human Services does not have a national plan," McDonald said. New York, which declared a state disaster emergency in response to its outbreak, recorded a measles-related child death - its first in over 30 years - earlier this month. Others say losing elimination status should itself prompt a strong response across all levels of government. "I do hope it's a wake-up call for CDC, for Congress, for HHS, for everyone," said Claire Hannan, the executive director of the Association of Immunization Managers. "We need to be doing more." A growing outbreak As the founder of a prominent anti-vaccine group, Kennedy had for years raised questions about the safety of the MMR vaccine. He previously linked the shot to autism despite decades of contradictory evidence. And he wrote in a book that measles outbreaks have been "fabricated" to "inflict unnecessary and risky vaccines" on millions of children. As the West Texas outbreak grew in early 2025, Kennedy coupled messages encouraging vaccination with false or misleading claims about the MMR vaccine. He promoted alternative treatments and questioned whether a child who state health officials said died of measles had actually died of the disease. His claims that vaccines contain "aborted fetus debris and DNA particles" prompted Debra Houry, the CDC's then-chief medical officer, to send information to "help him with his talking points," according to an email she sent to senior CDC officials on May 1, 2025. "Even though fetal cells are used to grow vaccine viruses, vaccines do not contain these cells or pieces of DNA that are recognizable as human DNA," she wrote to then-CDC chief of staff Matt Buzzelli and others. "Vaccines also do not contain fetal cells," she added. Kennedy's statements stood in contrast to how prior health officials messaged around vaccinations by imploring Americans to get vaccinated, including during President Donald Trump's first term. Then-Health Secretary Alex Azar said communities had been the subject of "mass disinformation campaigns. … They need to get their kids vaccinated." Public health experts say controlling outbreaks requires clear, repeated messages about vaccination, while acknowledging that declining trust in the CDC since the coronavirus pandemic has made federal officials less effective messengers. The CDC has not held a news briefing for reporters since Jan. 20, when the then-principal deputy director, Ralph Abraham, was asked whether losing elimination status would be significant and replied: "Not really. … You know, it's just the cost of doing business." The health department has maintained that Kennedy has "repeatedly stated that MMR vaccination is the most effective way to prevent measles infection" and that "any notion that the Trump Administration is discouraging measles vaccination is absolutely fake news." Two doses of the shot provide 97 percent protection against measles. Over the last year, dozens of measles outbreaks have taken hold across the country, and nationwide case counts have continued to climb. In West Texas, there were 762 cases during the 2025 outbreak. In South Carolina, the outbreak totaled 997 before it was declared over in April. And in Pennsylvania, officials have recorded 1,631 cases, including eight deaths, as of Friday. In July, the U.S. reported the most measles cases in 35 years, surpassing last year's record total. The resurgence, now totaling more than 5,800 cases nationwide, is posing myriad challenges for doctors and state health officials. Vaccine uptake has been declining for years amid rising skepticism. Meanwhile, outbreaks in traditionally undervaccinated communities are becoming harder to quickly extinguish. Many doctors have never seen cases of measles, prompting health departments to educate clinicians on the basics and hospitals to quickly craft new protocols to safely isolate patients with a virus that can remain suspended in the air for up to two hours. "Some of these outbreaks we've been seeing recently, for example, in Pennsylvania, it's not just kids who are getting sick," said Adriane Casalotti, who heads government and public affairs for the National Association of County and City Health Officials. "In fact, there's many more adults who are contracting measles, and that shows a longer pattern of undervaccination." When immunizations in the broader population are high, it's easier to protect communities with lower vaccination rates. But that's not necessarily the case anymore, Casalotti said. Pennsylvania has the largest measles outbreak in the country. But it's also been the center of a bitter political feud between Kennedy and Gov. Josh Shapiro, a Democrat widely viewed as a presidential contender. When Pennsylvania reported its first two measles-associated deaths in 35 years in August, Kennedy suggested the deaths "may even have been altogether fabricated," and he accused Shapiro of using the moment for political gain. It wasn't the first time Kennedy had disputed the official state account of deaths; he questioned whether measles caused the death of one of the two Texas children who died during the 2025 outbreak. Houry said such statements by Kennedy can leave the public with the impression that "maybe the disease isn't that deadly or that serious." The CDC's Schwartz made the unusual decision to exclude those first deaths from the national tally, departing from the agency's practice of relying on state health departments to make those determinations. The agency has since added some deaths from Pennsylvania and says it is working with outside partners to craft a new definition of deaths due to measles. The gap between federal and state counts has persisted as the toll has grown: States have now reported at least 11 measles-associated deaths this year in Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and New York. The CDC's tally is six. Can the U.S. regain its status? Kennedy's allies argue he should not be blamed for the rising cases of measles in the U.S., pointing to a worldwide resurgence and vaccine uptake that declined amid the covid pandemic. Other countries have lost their elimination status and regained it after years of work. Venezuela lost its status in 2018 and regained it in 2023. Brazil regained its designation in November 2024, about five years after losing it. Canada, which lost its status last year, has since stopped the continuous spread that cost it the designation, PAHO officials said. But it must go at least 12 months without measles spreading continuously before it can regain its status. State and local health officials say regaining elimination status will require a national strategy that accounts for widely varying conditions on the ground. States with large ongoing outbreaks, such as Pennsylvania, require a different response from places that have kept high vaccination rates and are trying to prevent the virus from gaining a foothold. In some communities where outbreaks are occurring, such as areas with Amish and Mennonite populations, some parents aren't necessarily opposed to vaccination or hesitant, but they don't get their children vaccinated because they don't routinely seek medical care. Yet some public health experts fear the rhetoric in the second Trump administration could dissuade parents from getting their children vaccinated. Kennedy's approach to vaccines is part of a broader push within the Trump administration to reduce and space out the shots children receive. While the administration has continued to recommend the MMR vaccine, Trump has suggested the combination vaccine could be "lethal," while acknowledging that he had no scientific evidence for the claim. He has said the vaccine should be broken up into three disease-specific shots, which medical groups say would offer no health benefit and could leave children vulnerable to more diseases for longer. The changes have been embraced by some activists in the MAHA movement that helped propel Kennedy into office even as major medical organizations have condemned them. That creates a difficult dynamic as Kennedy tries to regain a public health designation that depends heavily on increasing vaccination, public health experts say. The U.S. eliminated continuous measles transmission in 2000 through a combination of federal and state efforts, said Daniel Edney, president of the Association of State and Territorial Health Officials. States imposed vaccination requirements for schools, and the federal government created the Vaccines for Children program, which provides vaccines to about half the children in the U.S. "Everybody was pulling together the same way," Edney said. "There was no dissension. The medical community was in alignment with public health, who was in alignment with the CDC … and everybody was working toward the same goal." articles.title: At least 11 people killed in Mexico's Sinaloa after capture of cartel boss, officials say
articles.summary: GUASAVE, Mexico (AP) — A burst of violence in Mexico’s Sinaloa state after authorities captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,” left at least 11 people dead, authorities said Saturday. Meza Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, was captured and flown to Mexico City on Saturday after an intense firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen overnight left residents of the city of Guasave terrorized and trucks and businesses burning. Mexico’s Defense Ministry on Saturday afternoon said that seven alleged cartel gunmen and four Mexican soldiers were killed. The capo climbed the cartel ranks to lead the Beltrán Leyva cartel and later became the leader of his own group, the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization. The United States had a $5 million reward offer for information leading to his arrest, and he was wanted for trafficking drugs to the U.S. and illegally carrying firearms. Mexico's government said in a report early Saturday that intelligence from the Trump administration helped authorities capture him, but provided few details about how authorities in Mexico and the United States coordinated to detain Meza Flores. He was also a key ally to “Los Mayos,” a faction of the Sinaloa Cartel, which was designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the Trump administration last year. His capture represents a blow to the cartel as it fights with another faction for control of the northern Mexican state. Authorities in the United States and Mexico celebrated the arrest as a security win. U.S. President Donald Trump has pressured Mexico's government to go after criminal groups. As a fierce firefight settled into a tense calm Saturday, experts warned that picking off capos could set off another wave of violence in a region already caught up in a power struggle between warring cartel factions. Mexican forces' move against cartel fuels violence The capture of Meza Flores and his No. 2 in the city of Guasave, Sinaloa, set off a wave of violence when a firefight broke out around 7 p.m. on Friday, according to residents of the 290,000-person municipality. Soon, military helicopters and drones were flying overhead, and helicopters opened fire on key locations across the city. Videos show screaming civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, burning cars and businesses, and circling helicopters shooting at people below. Such shows of force by cartels are common following the capture or killing of leaders. “The fighting was happening all over Guasave,” said Alma Camacho, a Guasave resident and local journalist. “It spread throughout the city.” Mexican authorities said that they used “stealth and surprise” to arrest Meza Flores, establishing a security perimeter around the building where he was located. After coming under attack with guns and explosives from suspected cartel operatives, armed forces personnel entered a home and detained him. Video shared by Mexico's Defense Ministry shows Meza Flores and two others being marched by heavily armed soldiers onto a military aircraft to appear before prosecutors in Mexico City. A total of eight people were detained, according to authorities. Because of the violence, the Mexican army and National Guard special forces were unable to extract Meza Flores from Guasave until 4 a.m. on Saturday, said a federal official who spoke on condition of anonymity because he wasn’t authorized to discuss the case. “Getting him (Meza Flores) out was extraordinary,” the official said, describing an intense response by members of the criminal group who maintained at least “10 roadblocks” with burning vehicles on Guasave’s streets. Terror in Sinaloa Guasave resident and firefighter Paola Sánchez said that thousands of people were terrorized late Friday as they took shelter from intense gunfire in grocery stores and other locations. “Last night, many businesses were burned ... along with cars and trucks,” Sánchez told The Associated Press. She said that the city’s firefighters had to take shelter at their station and wait until Saturday morning for orders from their superiors to dispatch the first crews to check whether any businesses or vehicles were still burning. An uneasy calm seemed to settle over the city Saturday. Mexican Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch wrote on X on Saturday morning that armed forces would remain deployed in Sinaloa state to protect civilians. He lamented the deaths of the four soldiers killed in the operation. Burned-out trucks continued to line the freeway leading into the town, blocking roadways on Saturday. “The aftermath of last night’s war still lingers. Burned cars in the streets, several Oxxo stores completely burned down,” Camacho said, referring to a chain of convenience stores in Mexico. Guasave residents remained “very afraid” because security forces were absent from the streets, Camacho said. Capture prompts celebration and warnings Meza Flores' detention marks another high-profile capture of a cartel leader as Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum faces pressure from Trump to crack down on cartels. Sheinbaum has gone after illegal groups more aggressively than her predecessors, and homicides have dipped significantly in her two years in office. The U.S. and Mexican governments celebrated the capture on Saturday, with the DEA commending Mexican authorities. “Results like these don’t happen overnight. They are built on sustained cooperation and trust. This is what partners can accomplish together,” U.S. Ambassador Ronald Johnson said in an X post. “We will continue the hunt.” Mexican Security Secretary García Harfuch called the detention “an important step in pacifying Sinaloa.” Sheinbaum's government has targeted a number of cartel kingpins , including Jalisco New Generation Cartel leader Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes , known as “ El Mencho ,” who was killed by the military in February. Mexican security analyst David Saucedo said that the capture of Meza Flores marked another case of the governments of Mexico and the U.S. increasingly falling back on a longstanding security strategy that critics warn could fuel more violence in the long run. The so-called kingpin strategy relies on zeroing in on capos like Meza Flores as a way to combat cartels. But experts say that it often triggers violent power disputes among groups, like the one underway in Sinaloa. “What is evident is this is a product of pressure from the United States,” Saucedo said. “What they do is capture high-profile kingpins — the leaders — but they don’t dismantle the entire organization. They arrested the No. 1 and No. 2, but the entire network of hit men, street-level drug dealers, businesses and political and police connections remains intact.” ___ Janetsky and Sánchez reported from Mexico City. Associated Press writer Thomas Strong contributed to this report from Washington. articles.title: Jan. 6 leader who once backed Trump now says he's 'absolutely done'
articles.summary: IRVING, Texas (AP) — Stewart Rhodes didn’t just go to prison for Donald Trump . While serving time for his role in the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol, the founder of the right-wing militia known as the Oath Keepers got a tattoo of Trump’s defiant face after he survived an assassin’s bullet in Butler, Pennsylvania . It was further proof of Rhodes' devotion to the Republican president. But that's all over now. “I am absolutely done with Trump,” said Rhodes, sitting at a rickety yellow table outside a gastropub in Irving, Texas. He considers Trump not just a traitor, but "one of the very worst in our nation's history.” The repudiation from a former acolyte — one convicted of seditious conspiracy for orchestrating an ill-fated attempt to keep Trump in power six years ago — is another example of how allegiance to the president has faded even among extreme supporters. Back then, Rhodes claimed Trump lost the 2020 White House race to Democrat Joe Biden because of election fraud. This year in Texas, where Democrats had historic victories , he said there's another reason. “The lion’s share is because Trump pissed off his own base," Rhodes said, his face shaded by a black cowboy hat. An eye patch covers his left socket, the result of an old gun accident, and a glacial blue iris peers out from the other. Nearby, people mingled with drinks for his Christian Warriors After-Party, organized during a three-day conference called “Christ is King: America After Trump.” Some people approached to shake hands or sign up for the Oath Keepers or trainings for things like community defense and hurricane relief. ‘The first inkling’ of a split from Trump The beginning of Rhodes' break with Trump came when the president gave pardons to hundreds of people who were locked up for their actions on Jan. 6, 2021, but only commuted Rhodes' sentence . “That was the first inkling,” Rhodes said. Rhodes also said Trump's war with Iran violated Trump's promises to end foreign conflicts. And, Rhodes said, it felt like an affront when Trump dismissed people who urged his administration to release files about the Jeffrey Epstein case , calling them “PAST supporters.” Then Rhodes felt Trump went back on his longtime slogan. “We elected him to end the corruption in Washington, D.C. ‘Drain the swamp.’ Unfortunately his administration has been one of the most corrupt administrations in U.S. history," Rhodes said. “The pardons are pay-for-play and everything is pay-for-play.” The White House did not respond to a request for comment. Rhodes is not alone in his about-face on Trump, but there's an ideological through line, said Sam Jackson, an associate professor at the University at Albany with a focus on anti-government extremism. “They went from seeing Donald Trump as their ally in this fight against the conspiracy, to actually being co-opted by the conspiracy,” Jackson said, and it “points to deeper consistency in that understanding of the world as driven by hidden, evil actors.” Rhodes, who graduated from Yale Law School and worked for former U.S. Rep. Ron Paul of Texas, founded the Oath Keepers in 2009 with the goal of encouraging members of the military and law enforcement to resist what they view as unconstitutional orders, such as disarming citizens or carrying out warrantless searches. Watching from prison when Trump was fired on Rhodes later allied himself with Trump's political movement, and the Oath Keepers supported his attempt to remain in office after losing the 2020 election. Fueled with conspiracies about voter fraud, prosecutors said group members gathered weapons, organized trainings and assembled in Washington , where some helped storm the Capitol on Jan. 6. Rhodes, who did not enter the building that day, said he was a “political prisoner" who faced “illegality” in his trial. He was sentenced to 18 years, one of the longest sentences of any Jan. 6 case. “You are smart, you are charismatic and compelling and frankly that’s what makes you dangerous,” U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta said during the hearing. “The moment you are released, whenever that may be, you will be ready to take up arms against your government.” Rhodes was behind bars as Trump began his political comeback. He said he watched the assassination attempt in Butler on a prison television with other inmates. He saw Trump pump his fist and yell “fight,” and he figured that God’s hand was on the man. After Trump won the 2024 election, he swiftly pardoned hundreds of people convicted of crimes related to Jan. 6, including those who assaulted police officers. Rhodes received a commutation, which didn’t wipe his record clean. “He let us out of prison. We were grateful. I didn’t get a pardon though,” he said. Tattoo that honored Trump will be ‘modified’ to reflect a new reality The Justice Department vacated Rhodes' conviction earlier this year, lifting his felon status. Rhodes said he's working to rebuild the Oath Keepers, which previously had tens of thousands of members, according to leaked lists. With his rights restored, Rhodes said his first priority was to get some guns, and he didn't register to vote in time for the election. But he said he wouldn't have cast a ballot anyway. That's because Rhodes felt that “the Republican Party has taken us for granted," and he didn't want to choose between “a half a dose of poison or a full dose.” As for his tattoo of Trump, the man he now considers a traitor, Rhodes has plans that he didn't specify. “I will have this prison tattoo of Trump ‘modified,'” he wrote in a text message, “to reflect that reality. That treason.” This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/oath-keepers-founder-jan-6-130043975.html

articles.summary: 今年，美国投资级（IG）债券发行已创历史纪录，发行量达到1.88万亿美元。而明年IG债券总供应量预计将进一步攀升至2.1万亿美元。 然而，2027年存量债券到期规模约1万亿美元，叠加利率中枢上移推动年度票息收入升至5560亿美元，扣除到期与票息回流后的“净净”供给约5080亿美元，仍低于2020年峰值；净发行量1.06万亿美元仅占市场规模的11.2%，与11.0%的长期历史均值基本持平。高额到期与票息回流形成有效对冲，使总供给虽再创纪录，净吸收压力并未同步极端化。 供给结构明显向科技倾斜：预计2027年科技与媒体合计发行6120亿美元，约占全市场净发行量50%；其中AI相关融资约4500亿美元、同比增长64%，超大规模企业2250亿美元，数据中心与GPU融资合计2250亿美元。 AI资本开支由数据中心基建向芯片算力采购切换，融资期限显著缩短，超大规模科技公司正从长端向短端迁移。今年长端集中发行一度推陡信用利差曲线；但并购融资预计同比下滑52%至1440亿美元，期限多在5-7年的GPU融资将成为下一阶段主力，2027年IG发行将明显向前端与中段倾斜。 天量供给叠加 4.1万亿美元表外杠杆急剧膨胀 ，使AI融资成为悬在信用市场上空的房间里的大象。美联储鹰派立场推高实际收益率，但IG利差并未广泛走阔：JULI利差维持在100bp附近，BofA指数利差处于历史偏紧区间，收益率约6.26%，显示投资者仍具备吸收供给的能力；一级市场巨额发行主要靠IG公募基金与ETF创纪录流入、以及资金状况改善的企业养老金买盘承接。 2.1万亿美元总供给的表面压力能否超过净吸收能力，将决定美国信用市场是延续总量有韧性、结构分化的格局，还是走向更广泛的利差重定价。

articles.title: 郭明錤：谷歌将明年博通设计TPU出货量下调20%，计划增加联发科份额
articles.summary: 谷歌正在调整人工智能芯片采购策略，削减博通设计的高端TPU订单，同时计划增加联发科设计芯片的采购量。在数据中心电力供应和芯片产能双重受限的背景下，谷歌正重新分配算力资源。 据知名苹果及供应链分析师郭明錤最新行业调查， 谷歌已将博通设计的TPU 8i系列2027年出货量削减约100万颗，降幅约占该系列全年出货量的20%，其中定价较高的8i Max（代号Whalefish）受影响最大。 与此同时，谷歌计划提高联发科设计的TPU 8t系列出货量，但具体规模尚未确定。 这一调整可能给博通带来压力。作为谷歌TPU的核心设计合作伙伴，高端型号订单缩减或影响其定制芯片业务收入；联发科则有望借此扩大在谷歌AI基础设施供应链中的份额。 前沿模型优先，算力分配逻辑生变 郭明錤指出，谷歌近几个月多次强调，前沿模型开发将优先获得算力资源。此次调整TPU 8i与8t的采购组合，正是这一策略在供应链产能紧张和数据中心电力受限背景下的体现。 在资源约束下，谷歌倾向于将有限的高端算力集中用于前沿模型研发，而非继续扩大高价芯片的部署规模。 8i Max订单削减尤为明显，也反映出谷歌对芯片成本与算力资源配置的重新权衡。 与此同时，提高TPU 8t系列采购量，意味着谷歌希望通过调整芯片组合，在资源受限的情况下维持算力部署。联发科设计的8t系列最终增量仍未敲定，实际出货规模有待进一步观察。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.summary: 俄乌和平谈判重启，结束冲突的前景再度受到关注。 据媒体近日报道， 特朗普政府已向欧洲和乌克兰官员传达，希望基辅在明年1月初之前与俄罗斯达成和平协议，并通过近期一系列接触释放出强烈的时间紧迫感。 这一时间表令基辅担忧，乌克兰总统泽连斯基可能被迫接受一份以莫斯科条件为基础的协议。 据 新华社11月12日报道 ，俄罗斯总统普京当天在莫斯科会见美国总统特使威特科夫和特朗普女婿库什纳时表示，对俄方来说，任何外国军队在乌克兰驻扎都绝对不可接受，这会威胁俄安全，乌境内的外国军队是俄合法打击目标。威特科夫希望此次与普京会面能促成新一轮有欧洲方面代表参与的多方会谈。 特使威特科夫与库什纳本月在阿布扎比重启俄乌谈判，结束因中东冲突中断八个月的接触。此后，两人又先后前往莫斯科、都柏林和柏林，与俄乌及欧洲官员密集会晤。特朗普在与普京会面后称，后者已明确表示莫斯科“准备好实现和平”。 美方施压的影响已开始显现。乌克兰官员将Starshield（SpaceX星链的军用版本）近期受到的速率限制，以及“爱国者”拦截导弹交付延迟数月，视为美国削弱基辅谈判地位、迫使其让步的信号。 时间表背后的政治算术 推动这一时间表的核心是美国国内政治。 特朗普所属的共和党在本月中期选举中同时失去众议院和参议院控制权，民主党预计将加强对乌支持，并推动对俄罗斯采取更强硬措施。据报道援引四位知情人士，白宫因此希望在民主党接管国会前敲定协议。 尽管特朗普在和平谈判方面仍拥有广泛权力，民主党人仍可利用立法权增加对乌援助、推动对俄制裁，并通过国会监督调查特朗普的外交政策，以及威特科夫和库什纳的商业利益。 基辅对此尤为担忧。 据报道援引一位乌克兰高级官员，特朗普“喜欢普京，想在一月前把这一切了结”，并警告称，如果协议在这一期限前达成，俄罗斯“可能获得更好的条件”。 欧洲官员也表达了类似忧虑。 美方急、俄方不急 谈判双方的节奏明显不对称。据报道，一位欧洲官员在会见威特科夫和库什纳后表示： “美国人在使劲推，也有人担心，要接近达成协议需要乌克兰作出大量让步。” 另一位欧洲官员则直言： “美国人很着急，普京一点也不急。” 俄罗斯的核心要求并未松动。普京周四与特朗普会晤后表示，乌克兰及其欧洲盟友必须接受“妥协”和“现实”。俄方要求基辅交出顿巴斯前线关键地区，放弃加入北约，并限制乌克兰武装力量；同时要求北约从东翼撤回部队和武器部署，调整欧洲冷战后的安全秩序。 莫斯科也没有快速达成协议的明显动力。报道援引两位了解克里姆林宫思路的人士称，俄方计划继续通过空袭增加谈判筹码。此外，普京坚持将欧洲更广泛的安全问题纳入最终协议，而相关议题才刚开始进入谈判。 这意味着，除非乌克兰及其欧洲盟友作出重大让步，否则俄方接受美方推动的快速协议并不容易。 安全保障：一个尚未落地的构想 美方提出，可由西方国家参照北约第五条款的集体防御模式，为乌克兰提供安全保障。库什纳周四在柏林表示，他认为特朗普愿意接受这一方案，并称美方已让俄罗斯接受安全保障以第五条款为基础的概念。 但特朗普本人对此仍未给出明确承诺。周五被问及是否可能向乌克兰提供此类保障、是否与普京讨论过时， 他表示：“我们这边会发布一些东西，因为这也是一场公关战。”“我们会说一些话，他们也会说一些话。” 俄方则迅速表明反对立场。参加阿布扎比最新一轮谈判的俄罗斯副外长Sergei Ryabkov周五通过国际文传电讯社表示，即便是对基辅而言相当于准北约成员身份的安排，俄罗斯也无法接受。 他强调，乌克兰必须承诺永远不加入北约，只有这一要求得到满足，俄方才愿意讨论安全保障问题。 欧洲的席位与G20的悬念 欧洲国家主张先实现停火，再讨论更广泛的安全框架，并要求在谈判中获得正式席位。 俄罗斯虽承认欧洲需要参与最终协议，但普京尚未承诺扩大谈判范围，表示要等欧洲官员与俄方在莫斯科会晤后再作决定。 据报道援引两位官员透露，美国官员还提出，特朗普可能在下月于迈阿密举行的G20峰会上，与欧洲领导人讨论结束战争的方案。但一位法国高级官员表示，峰会期间不会就乌克兰问题与欧洲方面举行谈判，因为乌克兰并未受邀。 特朗普已邀请普京出席峰会，但这位俄罗斯领导人尚未表态是否参加。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 恒生科技指数迎史上最大调整：30只扩至50只，近300亿港元资金待配置
articles.summary: 11月20日，恒生指数公司发布今年第三季度恒生指数系列季度检讨结果。恒生指数、恒生国企指数、恒生科技指数及恒生综合指数的成份股变动将于2026年12月4日收市后实施，并于2026年12月7日起生效。 恒生指数成份股没有变动，成份股数目维持95只。恒生国企指数成份股数目维持50只，纳入智谱、MINIMAX-W，剔除邮储银行、申洲国际。 恒生科技指数成份股由30只扩容至50只，纳入建滔集团、瑞声科技、立讯精密、胜宏科技、禾赛-W、英诺赛科、中际旭创、迅策、宁德时代、金山云、壁仞科技、澜起科技、长飞光纤光缆、优必选等。 对此，业内人士认为，本次恒生科技指数成份股由30只一次性扩容至50只，新增名单覆盖先进硬件、光通信、算力、半导体、智能驾驶、机器人等赛道，或意味着恒生科技指数底层定位切换。 一名港股市场资深人士对记者表示，恒生科技指数已从“互联网平台指数”转向“泛硬科技指数”。“过去恒生科技指数可选消费行业占比较高，缺乏AI、算力、芯片股。新纳入股票以先进硬件、人工智能主题为主，这些调整有望进一步呈现当前港股科技产业全貌。”上述人士表示。 10月7日，恒生指数公司公布恒生科技指数编算方法修订方案的市场咨询总结。恒生指数公司表示，将从扩大科技主题覆盖、引入分组选股机制两方面修订指数。业内人士表示，这是恒生科技指数2020年发布以来最大的一次修订。 在扩大科技主题覆盖方面，恒生指数公司表示，将采纳早前提出的修订方案，取消合资格候选公司必须属于恒生行业分类系统五个指定行业的要求。 在采纳此前修订方案的基础上，恒生指数公司对恒生科技指数主题进行了整合与拓展，并新增了前沿科技主题。调整后的六大科技主题包括：数字平台与解决方案、人工智能、先进硬件、机器人及自动化、云计算以及前沿科技。同时，恒生科技指数的科技子主题由16个增至24个。 在选股机制上，恒生科技指数引入了分组选股机制。恒生指数公司采纳早前提出的修订方案，将选股范畴由主板上市公司修订至恒生综合大中型股指数成份股，并正式引入双组别选股机制。新机制分别以市值排名和收入增长排名作为选股准则，其中非现有成份股须满足过去三个月日均成交额不低于1亿港元的条件，按收入增长排名入选的个股则须在最近连续两个财政年度均实现至少5亿港元的年收入，从流动性和基本面两个维度设定了明确的准入门槛。 恒生科技指数50只成份股中，前40只按市值排名选取，侧重覆盖大市值龙头；剩余10只按过去12个月的收入增长排名选取，为具备高成长潜力的科技企业提供纳入空间。这一调整在扩大指数代表性的同时，也强化了科技主题投资的成长属性。 中信证券发布研报认为，恒生科技指数编算方案的修订主要由港股科技板块结构性变化引起。港股科技板块早期高度集中于互联网业务，近年来先进硬件与人工智能相关上市公司的数量显著增加，特专科技公司也陆续登陆市场。 “同时，港股科技板块收入增长较强的公司往往市值较小，在仅以公司市值为基础的选股框架下，高增长但规模相对较小的公司或未能被纳入指数。此次恒生科技指数编算方案修订的核心要义，在于使其成为更广泛、更具前瞻性的港股科技股基准指数。”中信证券认为。 此次修订对市场最直接的影响，是被动资金的大规模重新配置。 恒生指数公司数据显示，截至2026年9月底，被动式追踪恒生指数系列的产品资产管理总值约为1055亿美元，其中追踪恒生科技指数的资产管理规模已从2020年推出初期的15亿美元，增长至371亿美元。今年10月，广发证券发布研报表示，恒生科技指数新增成份股对应的配置需求约为291亿港元。 本文来源： 上海证券报 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: “脱欧”十年之后，英国又要“入欧”？
articles.summary: 脱欧十年之后，英国正站在是否重返欧盟的门槛上。首相伯纳姆‌本周五在布鲁塞尔公布一揽子协议，并明确提出英国应就是否回归这一重要贸易集团展开辩论——这让“脱欧、悔脱欧、再入欧”的政治链条第一次有了现实轮廓。 据《华尔街日报》近日报道，伯纳姆‌与欧盟方面达成的“重置”协议包括取消大部分食品和农产品边境检查、重启学生交流项目。 欧盟委员会主席Ursula von der Leyen称，这标志着英欧关系的“转折点”。伯纳姆‌则称，这是一份“双赢”协议，是“英国的好日子，也是欧洲的好日子”。 但协议落地仍存变数。 欧洲谈判代表明确表示，除非欧盟学生在英国大学能享受更低学费，否则协议不会全面执行，双方同意在未来六个月继续谈判。 伯纳姆‌也承认，这“很可能已是本届议会任期内能够达成的上限”。 对市场而言，信号意义大于短期经济效果。伯纳姆‌称，协议最多可为英国经济带来相当于GDP 0.5%的增量；高盛研究则显示，若英国重返欧盟单一市场，经济总量可能提升2%至5%。但重入进程漫长、成本不确定，英国可能由此面临持续数年的政治不确定性。 十年之后，民意天平倒向“回归” 2016年公投中，52%的英国选民选择脱欧，四年后英国正式退出欧盟。如今，多项民调平均显示，62%的英国人希望重返欧盟，38%希望留在欧盟之外。 伯纳姆‌本周直言：“我们得到的脱欧方案没有奏效。我们失去的比得到的多。” 这与前任斯塔默的谨慎路线形成对比。斯塔默于2024年带领工党重新执政后，主张“让脱欧运转起来”，通过有限协议和部分监管对齐降低贸易摩擦，但未能扭转政策方向。伯纳姆‌接任后，仅用四个月便在欧洲议题上展现出更鲜明的立场。 上月，伯纳姆‌表示希望在有生之年看到英国重返欧盟，但排除在本届议会任期内推动，同时突破工党2024年竞选纲领中不重返单一市场、不重返关税同盟、不恢复人员自由流动的“红线”。 他承诺在本次峰会后，启动与欧盟关于长期关系选项的讨论。 协议内容有限，症结仍在学费与规则让渡 本次峰会达成的成果具体而有限。据CNN报道，协议涵盖青年交流计划、碳排放交易体系对接以及削减食品贸易壁垒。其中，青年计划允许英欧各10万名年轻人在对方境内最多居留三年，用于工作、学习或旅行，预计不迟于2030年1月落地。 但协议全面实施仍受学费问题制约。据《华尔街日报》报道，欧盟谈判代表要求欧洲学生在英国大学享受与英国学生相近的低学费待遇。双方周五发布的联合声明称，将就此达成补充协议，预计在未来六个月内完成谈判。 规则让渡同样是争议焦点。 英国欧洲事务大臣Hamish Falconer向BBC承认，协议实施意味着英国必须接受欧盟产品监管规则，却无权参与制定。这正是脱欧辩论中长期存在的矛盾：英国希望减少贸易壁垒，却不愿放弃监管自主权。 重入路径多选项，但每一条都有代价 英国可能的重返路径主要有三种，各自对应不同程度的市场准入与主权让渡。 其一是加入关税同盟 ，实行统一对外关税、便利双边商品贸易，同时保留服务业监管自主权，但英国商品进入欧盟单一市场仍可能面临部分检查。 其二是参照挪威模式加入单一市场 ，接受欧盟规则、允许人员自由流动并缴纳相关费用，但无权参与规则制定。 其三是全面重返欧盟 ，承担更高会费并恢复人员自由流动，同时重新获得参与贸易集团决策的权利。 但英国未必能获得当年享有的特殊条件。报道指出，保留本币、享受会费折扣等原有优势都没有保证，而一旦这些条件无法延续，公众对重返欧盟的支持可能减弱。 智库“英国与变化的欧洲”负责人Anand Menon表示：“没有按钮能让你回到2016年。”他警告，重返议题可能长期占据政治议程，增加经济不确定性，并分散政府处理国内问题的精力。 “认为当初离开是个坏主意，并不等于认为现在应该加入。” 欧盟方面也并不急于推动。欧盟外交与安全政策高级代表Kaja Kallas上周表示，英国脱欧给欧盟造成了“大量创伤”，未来谈判“不会那么容易”。Carnegie Europe主任Rosa Balfour则指出，英国重返并非欧盟的首要议题，欧盟希望确认英国提出的新关系方案能够长期维持。von der Leyen虽然表示愿与英国就未来关系展开讨论，但也没有承诺具体时间表。 反对声浪重启，经济时机却略显尴尬 英国国内的反对力量正在重新集结。据《华尔街日报》报道，名为“Stay Out”的阵营已在社交媒体上大量投放内容。前首相鲍里斯·约翰逊称，伯纳姆‌会因此“把自己和工党钉死”；发起脱欧公投的前首相卡梅伦则呼吁政府优先处理税收、债务、住房和国防等国内问题。 保守党领袖Kemi Badenoch指责伯纳姆‌没有吸取过去的教训，改革党领袖Nigel Farage则称他没有获得与布鲁塞尔推动更紧密关系的授权。 YouGov调查显示，重返欧盟在选民优先事项中仅排第九，远低于经济、移民和医疗。 经济环境也让重返欧盟面临新的权衡。多数经济学家认为脱欧损害了英国经济，但也指出英国并未借此推进去监管和提升竞争力。与此同时，据《华尔街日报》报道， 英国近几个季度经济表现好于预期，部分得益于更快的AI应用。一些人士担心，欧盟更严格的AI监管可能限制这一增长动力。 民意支持与实际政策选择之间仍存在距离。民调研究机构Persuasion UK副主任Morgan Jones认为，如果英国明天就能按照2016年的条件重返欧盟，这一选项将获得压倒性支持，对工党争取不同群体选民也有吸引力。但她指出，预算分摊、加入欧元区的风险以及漫长的谈判过程，都可能让选民逐渐失去耐心。 articles.title: 国内反对、海外也不行？特朗普威胁对“海外建设数据中心”加重税
articles.summary: 美国AI基础设施投资面临新的政策与现实阻力，企业全球算力布局的不确定性进一步上升。 11月21日，据媒体报道，特朗普周五在白宫新闻发布室对记者表示： “我们不会允许我们的公司在美国以外建设数据中心。” 他称，美国此前允许企业在芯片等领域向海外转移产能，对美国造成了严重损害，因此不会允许类似情况在数据中心领域重演。 特朗普还表示， 美国将对试图在海外建设数据中心的企业征收“巨额税费”或施加其他惩罚。不过，他没有说明禁令将通过何种方式实施，也承认尚未与政府团队讨论这一计划：“我甚至还没跟我的人说过这件事。” 这一表态也凸显出美国AI基础设施建设面临的另一重矛盾：特朗普希望推动数据中心在美国扩张，但相关项目在美国国内正遭遇越来越多的社区反对。电力消耗、基础设施压力等问题，已经成为美国数据中心扩张面临的现实阻力。 政策细节尚不明确，国内数据中心建设也面临阻力 据报道，目前尚不清楚特朗普具体设想采取何种措施，以及如何落实这一禁令。白宫方面也未立即回应置评请求。 对美国科技企业而言，海外数据中心是全球算力布局的重要组成部分。土地、电力供应和建设成本等因素都会影响项目选址。 如果海外建设受到限制，企业可能需要重新调整投资计划，在美国本土寻找更多建设资源，也可能面临更高的基础设施成本。 与此同时，美国国内对数据中心扩张的反对声音持续上升。据媒体报道， 在今年的中期选举中，数据中心成为选民关注的重要议题，承诺限制数据中心扩张的候选人获得了明显支持。 随着相关项目增加，电力消耗、当地基础设施负担及社区影响引发越来越多争议。 特朗普此前多次反对州和地方政府限制数据中心建设，认为数据中心能够带来就业、税收和经济增长。 今年8月，他曾呼吁社区不要叫停相关项目，周五再次表示，应当让数据中心为当地社区创造收益，而不是将其关停。 AI交易承压，算力投资再添政策不确定性 特朗普的最新表态为AI产业带来新的政策风险。美国科技企业一方面需要持续扩大算力规模，另一方面可能面临海外建设受限、本土项目又遭遇地方阻力的双重约束。若相关限制落地，企业的全球数据中心选址和资本开支安排都可能受到影响。 这一政策风险出现之际，AI交易本身已显露疲态。标普500指数自11月4日以来累计下跌约9%，投资者对AI股票估值及投资回报的担忧持续升温。 即便Anthropic本周完成创纪录规模的IPO，也未能缓解市场对AI股票估值可持续性的忧虑。 特朗普此前曾对Anthropic及其Claude聊天机器人表示赞赏，但对AI产业的支持也伴随着对企业投资地点的限制要求。对于正大举投入数据中心建设的美国科技企业而言，海外布局与本土扩张都可能面临新的政策和现实约束。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: “文娱史上最成功发售，堪比007、星球大战、米老鼠”！GTA 6发行首日收入高达38亿美元
articles.summary: 《GTA 6》以创纪录的首日收入，成为文娱史上最成功的发行项目之一。 11月21日，据彭博，Take-Two Interactive旗下 Rockstar Games新作《Grand Theft Auto VI》（简称《GTA 6》）发售首日全球收入达到37.9亿美元 ，超过《复仇者联盟4：终局之战》约29亿美元的全球票房，也高于Taylor Swift“Eras”巡演约20亿美元的销售额。 美国银行分析师认为，《GTA》已成为与007、星球大战和米老鼠比肩的跨代际IP。 数据显示，《GTA 6》预售销量达到3250万份，创下游戏发行纪录。Sensor Tower数据显示，超过80%的预购玩家选择售价100美元的Ultimate Edition，而非80美元的标准版。 游戏发售首日还在直播平台掀起热潮。据CNN报道，玩家在Twitch、YouTube和Kick上的累计观看时长超过1.32亿小时，刷新直播平台纪录。 Take-Two股价周五盘中一度下跌，随后逆转收涨近1%，在科技股整体重挫的背景下跑赢大盘。 13年等待，首日收入达到前作4.7倍 《GTA 6》于11月19日正式发售，距离上一部正统续作《Grand Theft Auto V》已经过去13年。Rockstar为新作投入超过八年开发时间，目前拥有逾4700名员工。游戏以虚构的迈阿密“Vice City”为背景，围绕Jason和Lucia两名主角展开。 作为对比，《GTA 5》于2013年发售时，首个24小时销售额为8亿美元，三天内突破10亿美元。 《GTA 6》首日收入约为前作的4.7倍。据Sensor Tower数据，在正式发售前，该游戏已产生23.6亿美元收入，预售自6月开启，持续约五个月。 PC版与在线模式待推出，跨代际IP价值受关注 目前《GTA 6》尚未登陆PC平台。Take-Two表示，PC版本预计稍后推出，在线模式也在规划之中。这意味着PC端销售和线上业务的持续变现，仍有望成为后续收入来源。 美国银行全球研究部分析师Omar Dessouky指出， 此次发行推动《GTA》从一款电子游戏升级为与James Bond（007）、星球大战和米老鼠比肩的“跨代际IP”。更成熟的叙事有望重新吸引多年未接触游戏主机的玩家，而顶级画面与开放世界玩法则有助于吸引年轻用户。 Wedbush Securities分析师Alicia Reese表示，《GTA 6》为Rockstar构建更多游戏提供了新平台，未来数年都将令Take-Two受益。 发行热度也已延伸至游戏之外。Take-Two在迈阿密展开大规模营销，当地举办庆祝活动，NBA迈阿密热火的比赛也融入了游戏元素。Rockstar与PlayStation还计划在当地举办演唱会。随着感恩节假期到来，这款游戏有望继续推动假日季游戏消费。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
